svg.aria-label: Who owns what: a matrix of five cross-cutting rules against the three rows of the W5 set — FIX-1458, the held child epic FIX-1455, and the unfiled working-assemblies row. ER-1, a person occupies the same roster slot, is decided by FIX-1458 and consumed by both others. ER-2, Waiting-on-you is parked and Idle is runtime, is decided by FIX-1458 and consumed by both others. ER-3, the reference runs and survives a redeploy, is built by FIX-1455 and consumed by the assemblies row. ER-4, assemblies compose and add no layer, is conditional: a dashed cell under FIX-1455 reading BUILDS IF NOT CUT, and a dashed cell under the assemblies row reading BUILDS IF CUT. ER-19, the done condition, is likewise conditional: a dashed cell under FIX-1455 reading PROVISIONAL OWNER, and a dashed cell under the assemblies row reading OWNS IF CUT — FIX-1455 holds it unless the assemblies cut says otherwise, so the collapse path has a defined owner rather than none. Four of the five rules in the matrix have one committed owner; the fifth’s is provisional, which is the epic’s structural gap and is Open 2 and 3. Sixteen further rules sit outside this matrix because they bind every row equally and need no column: ten prohibitions, ER-5 to ER-14; four rules for how the set is run, ER-15 to ER-18; and two more proof rules, ER-20 and ER-21.
svg.text: WHO OWNS WHAT — FOUR RULES HAVE ONE OWNER; THE FIFTH’S IS PROVISIONAL

g.text: ER-4 · assemblies compose, add no layer
the one committed owner — decides or builds it
consumes it, and must not re-decide it — not a wait
provisional or conditional — a default place to look, settled by the assemblies cut, not a commitment
Only one column is live this cycle. FIX-1455 runs its own epic lifecycle; the assemblies column is not filed at all.
ER-19 is the epic's done condition. FIX-1455 holds it provisionally, unless the assemblies cut says otherwise — Open 2 and 3.
Sixteen further rules bind every row equally and need no column: ten prohibitions ER-5–14, four run-the-set ER-15–18, two proofs ER-20/21.
